Names in this guide: `subagent` is `Agent`, `skill` is `Skill`, and `mcp__papermemory__*` is `mcp__plugin_academic-harness_papermemory__*`. If a tool named below is not in your tool list, say so.

## Provenance audit

Before reporting, submitting, or answering "what supports this?", run `provenance_audit` `action: "index"` then `unsupported`: it joins the ledgers that already exist (review evidence, extraction, appraisal and GRADE events, `reporting_check` verdicts, stored `deep_review` claims, citation verdicts, and validity flags, notebook hypotheses, `analysis_run` expectations/re-executions/compliance, `experiment_log` protocol digests and verdicts, `ablation` attribution, dataset downloads, `meta_analysis` studies, and `ah` claim sidecars) by the ids and hashes they store, and is strictly read-only. Read its eleven states as recorded, never as verdicts: `no_link` means nothing was linked, `not_checked` means a quote was stored but never verified, `unverified` means a check did not confirm it, `stale` means the source behind the evidence changed, `not_found` means a recorded link has no far end, `spec_drift` means an experiment run changed its evaluation protocol against its baseline, `rerun_mismatch` means a declared reported value did not reproduce, `no_attribution` means an ablation attributes no component to the gain, and `verdict_missing` means a staged variant run or an ablation has no human verdict. A ledger it cannot read is reported `unknown` with its reason — say so instead of treating it as unsupported, and never present an unverified claim as supported. Use `arms` for one four-column readiness roll-up (reported vs recomputed, protocol digest, references, method–code) over artifacts that already exist — it is a reading, not an acceptance decision. Use `rollup` for the ordered loop record (frozen problem → limitations → idea pool → subset verdicts → scale-up → selection → ablation → review rounds with evaluator kind → integrity → incumbent): it is a report only, writes no promotion, lists unrecorded cost/time as missing rather than zero, computes no successful-cases-only headline, and shows whether the reproduced baseline was itself gated by `expect`/`verify_scores`. Use `impact` with a `paper:`, `quote:`, file, or `run:` id before editing or re-running anything it supports, `stale` after any source or manuscript changed, and `export format=markdown` (or graphml/mermaid) for an auditable attachment. Set `verify_quotes: true` only when PaperMemory is available and the user wants live re-checking. Load the `provenance-audit` skill.
